subject: maths
title: Place Value to 1,000,000, Counting in Powers of 10 and Negative Numbers
seo_title: Year 5 Place Value Worksheets: Numbers to a Million and Negative Numbers (Free)
standard_text: Read, write, order and compare numbers to at least 1,000,000 and determine the value of each digit; count forwards or backwards in steps of powers of 10 for any given number up to 1,000,000; interpret negative numbers in context, count forwards and backwards with positive and negative whole numbers, including through zero.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 maths worksheets for the National Curriculum: place value up to 1,000,000, numbers in words, counting in steps of 10, 100, 1,000, 10,000 and 100,000, comparing and ordering, and negative numbers through zero. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: In a 6-digit number, each digit is worth hundreds, tens or ones of thousands, or hundreds, tens or ones. The place decides the value.
key_sub: The 4 in 304,020 is worth 4,000. Write 0 in every empty place, change only one digit when you count in powers of 10 (exchange when a 9 goes up), and say 0 when you count through zero.
body_html:
Place value up to 1,000,000

A 6-digit number has two groups of three digits: thousands and ones. Each group has hundreds, tens and ones. Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right. 10 hundred thousands make 1,000,000 (one million).

Reading and writing big numbers

Read the thousands group and say “thousand”, then read the last three digits. In words we write “and” before the last tens and ones.

DigitsWords
304,020three hundred and four thousand and twenty
90,712ninety thousand, seven hundred and twelve
1,000,000one million
Words to digits

Write two hundred and fifty thousand and nine in digits.

Two hundred and fifty thousand → 250. Nine → 009 (no hundreds or tens, so write 0s).

Answer: 250,009

Counting in powers of 10

To count on or back in 10s, 100s, 1,000s, 10,000s or 100,000s, change the digit in that place. When a 9 goes up, exchange: 10 of one place make 1 of the next place.

Number10,000 more100,000 less
245,318255,318145,318
896,000906,000796,000
503,214513,214403,214
Exchange

What is 1,000 more than 39,600?

9 thousands + 1 thousand = 10 thousands. Exchange them for 1 ten thousand: 3 ten thousands become 4.

Answer: 40,600

Compare and order

First count the digits: a 6-digit number is greater than any 5-digit number. If both have the same number of digits, compare place by place from the left until two digits are different.

Compare

306,500 ☐ 360,050

Hundred thousands: 3 = 3. Ten thousands: 0 < 6.

Answer: 306,500 < 360,050

Negative numbers and counting through zero

Numbers below 0 are negative. We meet them in temperatures, below sea level and in lifts. When you count through zero, 0 is one of the steps.

Temperature

The temperature was −4 °C. It rose to 6 °C. By how many degrees did it rise?

4 degrees up to 0 °C, then 6 more degrees: 4 + 6 = 10.

Answer: 10 degrees

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Missing a zero placeholder (three hundred and four thousand and twenty → 34,020)Write each group as three digits: 304 | 020 → 304,020
Giving the digit, not its value (the 4 in 304,020 is 4)It is in the thousands place: 4,000
Changing the wrong digit (10,000 more than 245,318 → 246,318)Find the ten thousands digit: 255,318
Comparing the first digits only (99,850 > 100,400)Count the digits first: 100,400 > 99,850
Skipping 0 when counting through zero (2, 1, −1)Say 0: 2, 1, 0, −1

faq.q: What place value do Year 5 children need to know?
faq.a: Year 5 pupils read, write, order and compare numbers up to 1,000,000 and know the value of each digit. They count on and back in steps of 10, 100, 1,000, 10,000 and 100,000, and use negative numbers in context, counting through zero.

faq.q: How do you write 304,020 in words?
faq.a: Read the thousands group, then the rest: three hundred and four thousand and twenty. When you write it back in digits, put 0 in every empty place.

faq.q: How do you find 10,000 more or less than a number?
faq.a: Change the ten thousands digit by 1 and keep the other digits the same: 10,000 more than 245,318 is 255,318. If the digit is 9, exchange 10 ten thousands for 1 hundred thousand: 896,000 + 10,000 = 906,000.

faq.q: Do Year 5 children learn negative numbers?
faq.a: Yes. The National Curriculum asks Year 5 pupils to interpret negative numbers in context, such as temperatures, and to count forwards and backwards through zero, for example 2, 1, 0, −1, −2.

sets.title: Value of each digit up to 1,000,000 and numbers in words

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 3 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 3 thousands = 3,000. The digit is 3, but its value is 3,000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 9 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 9 ten thousands = 90,000. The digit is 9, but its value is 90,000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 7 is in the hundred thousands place, so it is worth 7 hundred thousands = 700,000. The digit is 7, but its value is 700,000.

items.q: In 174,683, which digit is in the ten thousands place?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. In 174,683 the ten thousands digit is 7, worth 70,000.

items.q: In 197,348, which digit is in the hundred thousands place?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. In 197,348 the hundred thousands digit is 1, worth 100,000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 3 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 3 ten thousands = 30,000. The digit is 3, but its value is 30,000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 4 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 4 hundreds = 400. The digit is 4, but its value is 400.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 2 in 372,159?
items.e: The 2 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 2 thousands = 2,000. The digit is 2, but its value is 2,000.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 2 in 23,561?
items.e: The 2 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 2 ten thousands = 20,000. The digit is 2, but its value is 20,000.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 8 in 841,236?
items.e: The 8 is in the hundred thousands place, so it is worth 8 hundred thousands = 800,000. The digit is 8, but its value is 800,000.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 5 in 350,716?
items.e: The 5 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 5 ten thousands = 50,000. The digit is 5, but its value is 50,000.

items.q: Which number has a 7 in the ten thousands place?
items.e: In a 6-digit number the ten thousands place is the 2nd digit from the left (5th from the right). In 675,428 the 7 is there, so it is worth 70,000.
Put each digit in its place and write 0 in every empty place: 500,000 + 3,000 + 80 + 2 = 503,082.

items.q: What number is 60,000 + 700 + 4?
items.e: Put each digit in its place and write 0 in every empty place: 60,000 + 700 + 4 = 60,704.

items.q: Which number is three hundred and four thousand and twenty?
items.e: Write the thousands part first: three hundred and four thousand → 304. Then the last three digits: twenty → 020. Fill every empty place with 0: 304,020.

items.q: Which number is seventy thousand, six hundred and five?
items.e: Write the thousands part first: seventy thousand → 70. Then the last three digits: six hundred and five → 605. Fill every empty place with 0: 70,605.

items.q: Which number is two hundred and fifty thousand and nine?
items.e: Write the thousands part first: two hundred and fifty thousand → 250. Then the last three digits: nine → 009. Fill every empty place with 0: 250,009.

items.q: How do you write 406,050 in words?
c: four hundred and six thousand and fifty
forty thousand, six hundred and fifty
four hundred and sixty thousand and fifty
items.e: Split 406,050 at the comma: 406 thousand, then 50. Say the thousands part and the word “thousand”, then the rest: four hundred and six thousand and fifty.

items.q: How do you write 90,712 in words?
c: nine hundred thousand, seven hundred and twelve
nine thousand, seven hundred and twelve
ninety thousand, seven hundred and twelve
items.e: Split 90,712 at the comma: 90 thousand, then 712. Say the thousands part and the word “thousand”, then the rest: ninety thousand, seven hundred and twelve.

items.q: In 330,000, how many times greater is the value of the first 3 than the value of the second 3?
items.e: The first 3 is worth 300,000. The second 3 is worth 30,000. 300,000 ÷ 30,000 = 10. Each place to the left is worth 10 times more. (270,000 is the difference, not how many times greater.)

items.q: What is 10,000 more than 245,318?
items.e: Only the ten thousands digit changes: 4 → 5. The other digits stay the same. 245,318 + 10,000 = 255,318.

items.q: What is 100,000 less than 708,452?
items.e: Only the hundred thousands digit changes: 7 → 6. The other digits stay the same. 708,452 − 100,000 = 608,452.

items.q: Count in 100s: 46,800, 46,900, 47,000, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 100 more than the one before. 47,000 + 100 = 47,100. Only the hundreds digit changes.
Each number is 1,000 more than the one before. 130,500 + 1,000 = 131,500. Only the thousands digit changes.
Each number is 10,000 more than the one before. 57,450 + 10,000 = 67,450. Only the ten thousands digit changes.
Each number is 100,000 more than the one before. 350,000 + 100,000 = 450,000. Only the hundred thousands digit changes.
Only the ten thousands digit changes: 3, 4, 5, 6. So each number is 10,000 more than the one before.
Only the thousands digit changes and it gets smaller: 8, 7, 6, 5. So the rule is take away 1,000.

items.q: 10,000 more than a number is 482,150. What is the number?
items.e: Work backwards. If 10,000 more than the number is 482,150, the number is 10,000 less than 482,150: 472,150.

items.q: 100,000 less than a number is 360,400. What is the number?
items.e: Work backwards. If 100,000 less than the number is 360,400, the number is 100,000 more than 360,400: 460,400.

items.q: What is 1,000 more than 39,600?
items.e: 9 thousands + 1 thousand = 10 thousands. Exchange them for 1 ten thousand: the 3 becomes 4 and the thousands digit becomes 0. 39,600 + 1,000 = 40,600.

items.q: What is 100 more than 64,950?
items.e: 9 hundreds + 1 hundred = 10 hundreds. Exchange them for 1 thousand: 4 thousands become 5 and the hundreds digit becomes 0. 64,950 + 100 = 65,050.

items.q: Count in 10s: 5,970, 5,980, 5,990, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more than the one before. 5,990 + 10 = 6,000. 9 tens + 1 ten = 10 tens: exchange them for 1 hundred. Now there are 10 hundreds: exchange them for 1 thousand.

items.q: What is 10,000 less than 503,214?
items.e: There are 0 ten thousands, so exchange 1 hundred thousand for 10 ten thousands. 10 − 1 = 9 ten thousands and 4 hundred thousands are left. 503,214 − 10,000 = 493,214.

items.q: What is 10,000 more than 896,000?
items.e: 9 ten thousands + 1 ten thousand = 10 ten thousands. Exchange them for 1 hundred thousand: 8 becomes 9 and the ten thousands digit becomes 0. 896,000 + 10,000 = 906,000.
Each number is 10,000 less than the one before. 105,200 − 10,000 = 95,200. 105,200 has 0 ten thousands, so exchange 1 hundred thousand for 10 ten thousands: 10 − 1 = 9.

items.q: Count back in 1,000s: 13,050, 12,050, 11,050, 10,050, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 1,000 less than the one before. 10,050 − 1,000 = 9,050. 10,050 has 0 thousands, so exchange 1 ten thousand for 10 thousands: 10 − 1 = 9.

items.q: Count in 10,000s: 482,000, 492,000, ☐, 512,000. What number goes in the box?
items.e: The numbers go up by 10,000 each time. 492,000 + 10,000 = 502,000. 9 ten thousands + 1 ten thousand = 10 ten thousands: exchange them for 1 hundred thousand. Check: 502,000 + 10,000 = 512,000.

items.q: What is 1,000 less than 100,500?
items.e: There are 0 thousands and 0 ten thousands, so exchange 1 hundred thousand for 9 ten thousands and 10 thousands. Take 1 thousand away: 100,500 − 1,000 = 99,500.

items.q: What is 100,000 more than 900,000?
items.e: 9 hundred thousands + 1 hundred thousand = 10 hundred thousands = 1 million. 900,000 + 100,000 = 1,000,000.

sets.title: Compare and order numbers up to 1,000,000

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 7 hundreds is more than 6 hundreds. So 45,762 > 45,672.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 100,400 has 6 digits and 99,850 has only 5, so 100,400 is greater. Big first digits do not matter when a number has fewer digits.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the ten thousands place: 6 ten thousands is more than 0 ten thousands. So 360,050 > 306,500.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 4 tens is more than 0 tens. So 781,240 > 781,204.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 1,000,000 there are 10 equal jumps, so each mark is 100,000. The arrow is 7 marks after 0: 700,000.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 300,000 to 400,000 there are 10 equal jumps, so each mark is 10,000, not 1,000. The arrow is 6 marks after 300,000: 300,000 + 60,000 = 360,000.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the thousands place: 3 thousands is more than 1 thousand. So 953,187 > 951,837. 953,187 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the ten thousands place: 8 ten thousands is more than 5 ten thousands. So 684,591 > 654,981. 684,591 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: 98,760 has only 5 digits, so it is the smallest, even though it starts with 9. Of the 6-digit numbers, compare from the left. The digits are the same until the ten thousands place: 2 ten thousands is more than 0 ten thousands. So 120,300 > 103,200. 120,300 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 7 hundreds is more than 1 hundred. So 625,791 > 625,179. 625,179 is the smallest.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the ten thousands place: 2 ten thousands is more than 1 ten thousand. So 621,435 > 612,345. 612,345 is the smallest.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: 99,999 has only 5 digits, so it is the smallest. Every 6-digit number is at least 100,000.

items.q: Which number is between 450,000 and 460,000?
items.e: Numbers between 450,000 and 460,000 have 4 hundred thousands and 5 ten thousands. 455,800 fits. 45,980 has only 5 digits, so it is much smaller.

items.q: Put 154,932, 145,239, 195,432 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 145,239 < 154,932 (ten thousands: 4 < 5). 154,932 < 195,432 (ten thousands: 5 < 9). So the order is 145,239, 154,932, 195,432.

items.q: Put 978,324, 983,724, 973,428 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 973,428 < 978,324 (thousands: 3 < 8). 978,324 < 983,724 (ten thousands: 7 < 8). So the order is 973,428, 978,324, 983,724.

items.q: Put 362,874, 326,478, 367,428 in order from greatest to smallest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 326,478 < 362,874 (ten thousands: 2 < 6). 362,874 < 367,428 (thousands: 2 < 7). So the order is 367,428, 362,874, 326,478.

items.q: 6☐4,500 > 674,000. Which digit could go in the box?
items.e: The hundred thousands are the same (6). Compare the ten thousands: the box must be 7 or more. 4, 5 and 6 are too small. 684,500 > 674,000.

items.q: 3☐,850 < 34,100. Which digit could go in the box?
items.e: The ten thousands are the same (3). Compare the thousands: the box must be 4 or less. If it is 4, compare the hundreds: 8 > 1, so 34,850 would be too big. 33,850 < 34,100.

items.q: Use each of the digits 4, 0, 7, 2, 9 and 5 once. What is the greatest 6-digit number you can make?
items.e: Put the biggest digit in the hundred thousands place, then the next biggest, and so on: 9, 7, 5, 4, 2, 0. The greatest number is 975,420.

items.q: Use each of the digits 3, 0, 8, 1, 6 and 5 once. What is the smallest 6-digit number you can make?
items.e: Put the smallest digits first, but a 6-digit number cannot start with 0. Start with 1, then 0, then 3, 5, 6, 8: 103,568. (013,568 is really 13,568, a 5-digit number.)

sets.title: Negative numbers in context and counting through zero

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: The arrow is to the left of 0, so the number is negative. Count back from 0: −1, −2, −3. The answer is −3.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: The arrow is to the left of 0, so the number is negative. It is 2 marks past −5: count −6, −7. The answer is −7.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: The arrow is to the left of 0, so the number is negative. It is 1 mark past −5: count −6. The answer is −6.

items.q: What temperature does the thermometer show?
items.e: The red line ends below 0, so the temperature is negative. Each mark is 1 degree. Count down from 0: −1, −2, −3, −4. It shows −4 °C.

items.q: What temperature does the thermometer show?
items.e: The red line ends below 0, so the temperature is negative. Each mark is 1 degree. Count down from 0: −1, −2, −3, −4, −5, −6, −7. It shows −7 °C.

items.q: What temperature does the thermometer show?
items.e: The red line ends above 0, so the temperature is positive. Each mark is 1 degree. It is 1 mark above 5: 6 °C.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: On a number line −6 is further left than −2, so it is smaller: −6 < −2. Below 0, the bigger the number after the minus sign, the smaller the number.

items.q: Put these temperatures in order from coldest to warmest: −3 °C, 4 °C, −8 °C, 1 °C.
items.e: The coldest is the furthest below 0: −8 °C, then −3 °C. Then the temperatures above 0: 1 °C, 4 °C. Order: −8 °C, −3 °C, 1 °C, 4 °C.

items.q: Which temperature is the warmest?
items.e: All four are below 0. The warmest is the closest to 0: −1 °C is only 1 degree below 0.

items.q: Count back in 3s: 8, 5, 2, ? What comes next?
items.e: The numbers go down by 3 each time. Count back 3 from 2, one at a time: 1, 0, −1. Remember to count 0. The answer is −1.

items.q: Count back in 5s: 15, 10, 5, 0, ? What comes next?
items.e: 5 less than 0 is 5 below zero, so it is −5. Do not forget the minus sign: 5 is above zero.

items.q: Count on in 3s: −11, −8, −5, ? What comes next?
items.e: The numbers go up by 3 each time. Count on 3 from −5, one at a time: −4, −3, −2. The answer is −2.

items.q: Count on in 3s: −7, −4, −1, ? What comes next?
items.e: The numbers go up by 3 each time. Count on 3 from −1, one at a time: 0, 1, 2. Remember to count 0. The answer is 2.

items.q: Count on 7 from −3. Where do you land?
items.e: Count on 7 from −3: −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. Do not skip 0. The answer is 4.

items.q: Count back 6 from 2. Where do you land?
items.e: Count back 6 from 2: 1, 0, −1, −2, −3, −4. Do not skip 0. The answer is −4.

items.q: Count back 8 from 5. Where do you land?
items.e: Count back 8 from 5: 4, 3, 2, 1, 0, −1, −2, −3. Do not skip 0. The answer is −3.

items.q: Count on 5 from −8. Where do you land?
items.e: Count on 5 from −8: −7, −6, −5, −4, −3. You stay below 0. The answer is −3.

items.q: The dots show −4 and 6. How many steps apart are they?
items.e: Count in two jumps through 0. From −4 to 0 is 4. From 0 to 6 is 6. 4 + 6 = 10. Do not work out 6 − 4.

items.q: The dots show −5 and 3. How many steps apart are they?
items.e: Count in two jumps through 0. From −5 to 0 is 5. From 0 to 3 is 3. 5 + 3 = 8. Do not work out 5 − 3.

items.q: How many steps is it from −7 up to −2 on a number line?
items.e: Both numbers are below 0. Count up from −7: −6, −5, −4, −3, −2. That is 5 steps.

sets.title: Place value and negative number word problems

items.q: A house is for sale for £385,450. What is the value of the digit 8 in the price?
items.e: 385,450 has 3 hundred thousands, 8 ten thousands, 5 thousands, 4 hundreds, 5 tens and 0 ones. The 8 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth £80,000.

items.q: Which of these house prices is the highest?
items.e: £94,995 has only 5 digits, so it is the lowest. The others all have 4 hundred thousands. £490,500 and £490,050 have 9 ten thousands; compare the hundreds: 5 > 0. £490,500 is the highest.

items.q: A shop has four freezers. Their temperatures are −18 °C, −21 °C, −15 °C, −19 °C. Which is the coldest?
items.e: The coldest temperature is the one furthest below 0. −21 °C is 21 degrees below 0, more than any of the others.

items.q: Kai thinks of a number. It has 4 hundred thousands, 0 ten thousands, 7 thousands, 0 hundreds, 3 tens and 5 ones. What is his number?
items.e: Write the digits in order: 4, 0, 7, 0, 3, 5 → 407,035. The zeros keep every digit in the right place.

items.q: Grace is diving. She is 8 m below sea level (−8 m). She swims up 5 m. Where is she now?
items.e: Swimming up means count up. From −8 count up 5: −7, −6, −5, −4, −3. She is still below sea level: −3 m.

items.q: In a shopping centre the ground floor is level 0. The car park levels below it are level −1, level −2 and level −3. Charlie gets into the lift on level 2 and goes down 4 levels. Which level is he on now?
items.e: Count down 4 from level 2: 1, 0, −1, −2. Do not skip level 0. He is on level −2.

items.q: A football club’s total attendance for the season was two hundred and six thousand and forty. How is this written in digits?
items.e: Two hundred and six thousand → 206. Forty → 040 (no hundreds, so write 0). Fill every empty place with 0: 206,040.

items.q: At the 2021 census, Leeds had a population of 811,953. How is this number written in words?
c: eight hundred and eleven thousand, five hundred and ninety-three
eight hundred and eleven thousand, nine hundred and thirty-five
eighty-one thousand, nine hundred and fifty-three
eight hundred and eleven thousand, nine hundred and fifty-three
items.e: Split at the comma: 811 thousand, then 953. Say “eight hundred and eleven thousand”, then “nine hundred and fifty-three”.

items.q: Jack has the digit cards 0, 4, 7, 2, 9 and 6. He uses each card once to make the smallest 6-digit number he can. What number does he make?
items.e: Put the smallest digits first, but a 6-digit number cannot start with 0. Start with 2, then 0, then 4, 6, 7, 9: 204,679. (024,679 is really 24,679, a 5-digit number.)

items.q: Three concerts sold 65,407, 65,740, 65,074 tickets. Which list shows these numbers from smallest to greatest?
items.e: All three have 65 thousand. Compare the hundreds: 0 < 4 < 7. Order: 65,074, 65,407, 65,740.

items.q: A school website had 245,000 visits last year. This year it had 100,000 more. How many visits did it have this year?
items.e: 100,000 more: only the hundred thousands digit changes. 2 → 3. 245,000 + 100,000 = 345,000.

items.q: A town had a population of 99,400. Five years later it had grown by 1,000 people. What is the population now?
items.e: 9 thousands + 1 thousand = 10 thousands, so exchange for 1 ten thousand. Then 9 + 1 = 10 ten thousands, so exchange again for 1 hundred thousand. 99,400 + 1,000 = 100,400.

items.q: At the 2021 census, Cardiff had a population of 362,400. Which digit is in the ten thousands place?
items.e: Read the places from the left: 3 hundred thousands, 6 ten thousands, 2 thousands, 4 hundreds. The ten thousands digit is 6.

items.q: These are the populations of four cities at the 2021 census: Sheffield 556,521; Bristol 472,465; Leeds 811,953; Manchester 551,938. Which list orders the cities from greatest to smallest population?
items.e: Leeds is the only one with 8 hundred thousands, and Bristol has only 4. Sheffield and Manchester both have 5 hundred thousands and 5 ten thousands; compare the thousands: 6 > 1. Order: Leeds, Sheffield, Manchester, Bristol.

items.q: One winter morning in Aberdeen the temperature was −5 °C at 6 am. By noon it was 4 °C. By how many degrees did the temperature rise?
items.e: Count up in two jumps through 0. From −5 °C to 0 °C is 5 degrees. From 0 °C to 4 °C is 4 degrees. 5 + 4 = 9 degrees. (5 − 4 = 1 is the mistake of not crossing 0.)

items.q: The average distance from the Earth to the Moon is 384,400 km. What is the value of the digit 3?
items.e: The 3 is in the hundred thousands place, so it is worth 300,000 km.

items.q: A theme park had 300,000 visitors by the end of May, 400,000 by the end of June and 500,000 by the end of July. The total goes up by 100,000 each month. By the end of which month will it reach 900,000?
items.e: Count on in 100,000s: August 600,000, September 700,000, October 800,000, November 900,000.

items.q: A stadium had 58,900 fans at one match. At the next match there were 10,000 more fans. How many fans were at the next match?
items.e: 10,000 more: only the ten thousands digit changes. 5 ten thousands → 6 ten thousands. 58,900 + 10,000 = 68,900 fans.

items.q: A charity wants to raise £1,000,000. It has raised £960,000 so far. It raises £10,000 each week. How many more weeks will it take to reach £1,000,000?
At 4 pm the temperature was 2 °C. By midnight it had fallen by 6 degrees. What was the temperature at midnight?
items.e: Fallen means count down. From 2 count down 6: 1, 0, −1, −2, −3, −4. Do not skip 0. It was −4 °C.
